content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from various studies, reviews, and guidelines related to HIV treatment, antiretroviral therapy (ART), adherence, and associated outcomes. 1. A study conducted in the Amazon region of Brazil, published in PLoS One in 2015, explored specific aspects of HIV treatment and outcomes (10(4): e0121400). 2. Ford N, Meintjes G, Pozniak A, Bygrave H, Hill A, Peter T, and colleagues discussed the evolving role of CD4 cell count in monitoring antiretroviral therapy in a 2015 article in The Lancet Infectious Diseases (15(2): 241–247). 3. Vojnov L and the Clinton Health Access Initiative examined whether returning early infant diagnosis (EID) results via SMS/GPRS printers was more effective than routine result retrieval for HIV-exposed infants under 18 months in a 2015 study. 4. Violari A, Cotton MF, Gibb DM, Babiker AG, Steyn J, Madhi SA, and colleagues investigated the impact of early antiretroviral therapy on mortality among HIV-infected infants in a 2008 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine (359(21): 2233–2244). 5. The International Community of Women Living with HIV (ICW) and the Global Network of People Living with HIV (GNP+) conducted a study to understand the perceptions, values, and preferences of women living with HIV regarding early infant diagnosis in Kenya, Namibia, and Nigeria, accessed in January 2016. 6. Fox MP and Rosen S performed a systematic review of patient retention in antiretroviral therapy programs up to three years after treatment initiation in sub-Saharan Africa, covering the period from 2007 to 2009, published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2010 (15(s1): 1–15). 7. Rosen S and Fox MP reviewed retention in HIV care between testing and treatment in sub-Saharan Africa in a 2011 article in PLoS Medicine (8(7): e1001056). 8. Penn A, Azman H, Horvath A, Taylor K, Hickey M, Rajan J, and colleagues conducted a systematic review of interventions aimed at improving retention in ART programs for people with HIV in resource-limited settings, as outlined in a PROSPERO protocol. 9. Grimwood A, Fatti G, Mothibi E, Malahlela M, Shea J, and Eley B demonstrated that community adherence support improved program retention among children on ART in a multicenter cohort study in South Africa, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012 (15: 17381). 10. The World Health Organization (WHO) released consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, emphasizing a public health approach, accessed in November 2015. 11. Luque-Fernandez MA, Van Cutsem G, Goemaere E, Hilderbrand K, Schomaker M, Mantangana N, and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of patient adherence groups as a care model for stable ART patients in Khayelitsha, Cape Town, South Africa, in a 2013 PLoS One article (8: e56088). 12. Braitstein P, Siika A, Hogan J, Kosgei R, Sang E, Sidle J, and colleagues proposed a clinician-nurse model to reduce early mortality and improve clinic retention among high-risk HIV-infected patients initiating combination ART, published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012 (15: 7). 13. Hall BJ, Sou KL, Tucker JD, and Beanland RL reviewed barriers and facilitators to interventions aimed at improving HIV retention in care, as part of a qualitative evidence review in 2015. 14. Geldsetzer P and Bärnighausen T conducted a systematic review of interventions to improve retention of women in HIV care during the postpartum period, published by the Harvard School of Public Health in 2015. 15. Catalani C, Philbrick W, Fraser H, Mechael P, and Israelski DM systematically reviewed the literature on mHealth applications for HIV treatment and prevention, as published in the Open AIDS Journal in 2013 (7: 17–41). 16. WHO published guidelines on HIV disclosure counseling for children up to 12 years of age, accessed in November 2015. 17. Beckham S, Baral S, Negussie E, Doherty M, and Beyrer C conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of gender differences in HIV treatment outcomes, focusing on mortality, in a 2015 study. 18. Bangsberg DR, Perry S, Charlebois ED, Clark RA, Robertson M, and Zolopa AR demonstrated that non-adherence to highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) predicts progression to AIDS in a 2001 study published in AIDS (15(9): 1181–1183). 19. Nachega JB, Hislop M, Dowdy DW, Chaisson RE, Regensberg L, and Maartens G examined adherence to non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor-based HIV therapy and virologic outcomes in a 2007 Annals of Internal Medicine article (146(8): 564–573). 20. Wood E, Hogg RS, Yip B, Harrigan PR, O’Shaughnessy MV, and Montaner JS analyzed the impact of CD4 cell count thresholds on ART outcomes in a 2003 Annals of Internal Medicine study (139(10): 810–816). 21. Mills EJ, Nachega JB, Bangsberg DR, Singh S, Rachlis B, Wu P, and colleagues reviewed barriers and facilitators to HAART adherence in developed and developing nations in a 2006 PLoS Medicine article (3(11): e438). 22. Martin S, Elliott-DeSorbo DK, Wolters PL, Toledo-Tamula MA, Roby G, and Zeichner S identified patient, caregiver, and regimen characteristics associated with adherence to HAART among HIV-infected children and adolescents in a 2007 Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal article (26(1): 61–67). 23. Nachega JB, Uthman OA, Anderson J, Peltzer K, Wampold S, Cotton MF, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of ART adherence during and after pregnancy in low-, middle-, and high-income countries, published in AIDS in 2012 (26(16): 2039–2052). 24. Colvin CJ, Konopka S, Chalker JC, Jonas E, Albertini J, Amzel A, and colleagues systematically reviewed health system barriers and enablers for ART among HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women in a 2014 PLoS One article (9(10): e108150). 25. Hodgson I, Plummer ML, Konopka SN, Colvin CJ, Jonas E, Albertini J, and colleagues reviewed individual and contextual factors affecting ART initiation, adherence, and retention for HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women in a 2014 PLoS One article (9(11): e111421).
